sections.title: What does it mean?
sections.content: A basic Hungarian sentence can be very simple: a subject, a verb, and sometimes an object or other information. At this stage, focus on clear neutral statements and questions rather than advanced word order.

sections.title: How does it work?
sections.content: A simple statement can put the subject before the verb: Anna tanul. A yes/no question can use the same words with question intonation: Anna tanul? Negation uses nem before the verb: Anna nem tanul.

sections.title: Why does it look like this?
sections.content: Hungarian does not need a separate word equivalent to English do in a basic yes/no question. The same words can become a question through intonation and context. Negation is marked by nem before the verb.
Do not automatically add a Hungarian equivalent of English “do” when asking a simple yes/no question. Start with the same words and use question intonation.
